newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks open higher as rate fears diminish.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks open higher as rate fears diminish.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE
NIKKEI 18698.07 -37.40 LME CASH NICKEL US$7301 +1.0
CANDLR 1.3919 LME CASH ALUM US$1574.0 +57.0
CAN 30-YR 108.37 +0.07 BRENT CRUDE US$18.16 +0.10
* Toronto stocks opened higher across the board on Thursday, buoyed by positive earnings news. * Analysts said investors' fears of rising interest rates and inflation are diminishing.
Toronto stocks opened higher on Thursday, aided by positive corporate earnings and increased confidence that inflation and interest rates were under control.

"I think the realization is that the economy continues to plod along at a sustainable level, inflation is still under control... and investment alternatives continue to favor common share investments," said investment adviser Ira Katzin at RBC Dominion Securities.
In early action, the TSE 300 Composite index rose 32.16 points to 5906.29 in turnover of 11.13 million shares.
Total trading value was C$137.16 million. Advances outpaced declines 228 to 135, while 179 issues held their ground.
Katzin said high-quality stocks would be boosted by investors seeking refuge from jittery markets.

"Investors are not going to be hoodwinked as they used to be with the volatility in the markets, and they're going to buy when the market is down and beef up their positions in the high-quality issues," said Katzin.
All but one of Toronto's 14 sub-indexes rose in early trade, led by transportation, conglomerates and industrials.
The gold sector was the lone loser, shedding 67.24 points or 0.75 percent to 8896.21.
--- HOT STOCKS ---
* Bre-X Minerals Ltd shares were up 0.33 to 3.95 in heavy early session volume, continuing Wednesday's climb.
* Canadian National Railway shares rose 2.60 to 52.30 in healthy trade after CN said on Wednesday it expected improved operating performance in 1997.
* Moore Corp shares gained 1.20 to 29.50 in turnover of more than 500,000 shares after Moore reported higher earnings after Wednesday's close.
